newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul firms in talks with European jet consortium.
newsitem.headline: Seoul firms in talks with European jet consortium.

text.p: Four South Korean companies are in talks with a European aerospace consortium on cooperating in the development of a 70-seat passenger jet, a Samsung Aerospace Industries Co Ltd official said on Tuesday.

Samsung, Daewoo Heavy Industries Ltd, Korean Air Co Ltd and Hyundai Space and Aircraft Co Ltd are in talks with Aero International (Regional), made up of France's Aerospatiale, Alenia of Italy and British Aerospace Plc, he said.
"We are discussing the matter and no agreement of any kind has been reached yet," the public relations official told Reuters.
The official, who declined to be named, said further details were unavailable at this time.

The South Korean consortium has been actively seeking partners after a bid to takeover bankrupt Dutch plane-maker Fokker NV collapsed. The South Korean government had sent a faxed message to the Dutch Ministry of Economic Affairs ruling out a takeover bid from the consortium.

Fokker was declared bankrupt in March after racking up huge losses but was kept alive on a skeleton staff of 650 by court-appointed receivers in hopes of finding a buyer to salvage the company founded in 1919.
Dutch media had reported that the Samsung-led consortium had decided the problems involved in a takeover were just too large.
A South Korean-China agreement to develop 100-seat jets also failed last year.
